summary: The study investigates the absence of magnetism in hafnium oxide (HfO2) and hafnium silicate (HfSiO) films deposited by atomic layer deposition (ALD) and metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD). The results show that pristine HfO2 and HfSiO films are nonmagnetic, but contamination from stainless-steel tweezers during handling introduces ferromagnetic behavior. The study highlights that the observed magnetism is due to metallic contamination rather than intrinsic properties of HfO2.
evidence: ALD was carried out using alternating exposures of the common precursors HfCl4 and H2O in an N2 carrier gas. The temperature during the mounting procedure was measured by thermocouple to be approximately 40 °C. The authors note that contamination arising from handling by stainless-steel tweezers gave rise to noticeable levels of magnetism.
